classification.difficultyReason: Read horizontal-line intersections, then generalise the solution count using the maximum value 9 and explain why intersection x-coordinates solve f(x)=k. Earlier parts scaffold this connection.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows the graph of $f(x)=6x-x^2$. Copy this diagram into your book.

spec.description: Downward blue parabola, positive-axis arrowheads, unit ticks, x label only at 3, y labels 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10, dashed vertex guides, vertex label and downward curve-end arrows. No grid. Ordinary source grey marks become black under house style.
spec.mathematics: f(x)=6x-x^2 has vertex (3,9) and zeros 0 and 6.
spec.answerVisibility: The given graph contains no added horizontal response lines or intersection answers.

children.label: a
children.prompt: On your diagram, draw the line $y=8$. At what $x$-coordinates does the graph of $y=f(x)$ intersect the line $y=8$?

answer.worked: Draw the horizontal line $y=8$. Its intersections with the parabola are $(2,8)$ and $(4,8)$, so the required $x$-coordinates are $2$ and $4$.

spec.description: Complete self-contained supplied graph with the requested red horizontal line y=8 and dashed vertical read-off guides to newly labelled x ticks 2 and 4.
spec.mathematics: The horizontal line y=8 meets f(x)=6x-x^2 at x=2 and x=4.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many solutions does the equation $f(x)=8$ have?

answer.worked: The line $y=8$ intersects the parabola twice, so $f(x)=8$ has 2 solutions.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Using your diagram, how many solutions would you expect the equation $f(x)=6$ to have?

answer.worked: The horizontal line $y=6$ meets both sides of the parabola below its maximum, so $f(x)=6$ has 2 solutions.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Using a similar technique, how many solutions would you expect $f(x)=10$ to have?

answer.worked: The parabola has maximum value $9$. The horizontal line $y=10$ lies above it and has no intersections, so $f(x)=10$ has no solutions.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Consider the more general equation $f(x)=k$. For what values of $k$ would $f(x)=k$ have

answer.worked: At $k=9$, the horizontal line $y=k$ meets the parabola only at its vertex.
For $k<9$, the horizontal line $y=k$ lies below the maximum and meets the parabola twice.
For $k>9$, the horizontal line $y=k$ lies above the maximum and has no intersections with the parabola.

children.label: f
children.prompt: Make a general statement about the relationship between the equation $f(x)=k$ and the graphs of $y=f(x)$ and $y=k$.

answer.short: The solutions of $f(x)=k$ are the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points of $y=f(x)$ and $y=k$.
answer.worked: At an intersection, both graphs have the same $y$-value, so $f(x)=k$. Each intersection therefore gives a solution equal to its $x$-coordinate. The number of solutions equals the number of intersection points.
